pr_body:
## Description:

Currently Samsung TV power detection is implemented sending a fake KEY to samsungctl (the underlying component that controls the TV). This has the drawback that the samsungctl logs an info message.
This PR changes the state detection not sending any key but only recreating the connection 

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #25675 
**Pull request with documentation for [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io) (if applicable):** home-assistant/home-assistant.io#<home-assistant.io PR number goes here>

## Example entry for `configuration.yaml` (if applicable):
```yaml

```

## Checklist:
  - [x] The code change is tested and works locally.
  - [x] Local tests pass with `tox`. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass**
  - [x] There is no commented out code in this PR.
  - [x] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist]

If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed:
  - [ ] Documentation added/updated in [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io)

If the code communicates with devices, web services, or third-party tools:
  - [ ] [_The manifest file_][manifest-docs] has all fields filled out correctly. Update and include derived files by running `python3 -m script.hassfest`.
  - [ ] New or updated dependencies have been added to `requirements_all.txt` by running `python3 -m script.gen_requirements_all`.
  - [ ] Untested files have been added to `.coveragerc`.

If the code does not interact with devices:
  - [ ] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works.

[dev-checklist]: https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/development_checklist.html
[manifest-docs]: https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/creating_integration_manifest.html

I easily fixed many of them in my dev environment.

I don't know yet is that is problem of the tests or a real problem in the modified  code. 
IMHO the update method should invoke directly the get_remote (with state detection) and not the send_key as it is doing now. And the send_key should simply send keys.

```python
    # old
    assert remote.control.call_count == 2
    assert remote.control.call_args_list == [call("KEY_VOLUP"), call("KEY")]
    # new
    assert remote.control.call_count == 1
    assert remote.control.call_args_list == [call("KEY_VOLUP")]
```

> IMHO the update method should invoke directly the get_remote (with state detection) and not the send_key as it is doing now. And the send_key should simply send keys.
> I try to implement this and see how it works. I'll let you know.

> PS:Do you have a legacy samsungtv? (I've only websocket ones)

Yes.

@escoand as you can see I do am brave ;)
In this commit I commented the 5 failing tests (out of 42). This was mainly to see the coverage part.

As you can see there now 3 places in the code where same exception handling takes place:
* `send_key` as it was before my changes
* `get_remote `in the autodetect stuff as it was before
* `update`: my new entry
I don't like it that much.... well... I didn't even like the original code where the exception handling was in 2 part.
My idea is to put this stuff in a common function that gets the remote and if invoked in the `send_key` calls the control method. 
What do you think?

Can you please check if everything works in your real legacy tv? Thanks.

Hello @escoand, I know you're quite busy with your config flow PR. But have you had the time to check this one?
I did some tests on my samsung websocket TV and when I was in autoconfig mode (i.e. no port specified in the config) I got some timeout exceptions in the update method.
Last commit handles this exception.
I noticed this timeout exception while i was changing power state of the TV using the remote (switchig the TV on and off to see how fast HA was reacting).
Despite this exception I noticed also that HA looks faster in detecting the state change when the port is specified in the config.

Having notified this i tried to do the same state switching test against the current released code (HA 0.103.5) and I found that when no port is specified in the config HA reacts to the poweron event BUT if you switch off the television the state remains ON. the `self.get_remote().control(key)` does'nt raise any exception. If port is specified the problem does not occurs.
This PR fixes also this behavoiur.
How do we proceed with the 5 failing tests? Can you help me?
Thanks,
 Paolo

review_comments: This will not happen because you're already catching within `get_remote`. Same for some catches in `send_key`.
One solution could be to catch only in `get_remote` or have all exceptions cached in `update` AND `send_key` but not in `get_remote`.

@escoand I do not agree. `get_remote` is doing exception handling only in the autoconfig part. During normal operation mode there is no handling at all.
Doing catching only in `get_remote` will remove catching only from `update` but not from `send_key` (due to the `control` method).
While I was developing this PR I thought about a samsungctl bridge function where to put all exception handling that could be called from `update `and `send_key `but writing code I changed my mind going for the faster solution (so putting exception handling also in the `update`).
I'll leave this part unchanged. What do you think?
Obviously I have to admit you're right. So yes, leave it as it is.

The idea behind `self._power_off_in_progress` was probably the state doesn't switch off and on again because TV is still "in progress". Switching the state here doesn't make much sense to me. Better would be for me set the state in `turn_off` and `return` here as long it's still in progress. After this time we check again if it's `on` again.

Honestly I don't know... Maybe the clean thing is to set `self._state` only in the `update` method and remove it from the `send_key`. AFAIK the update is always called after the `send_key `calls so it's useless to set it there if the `update `will set it again, right?
Not sure but while reading you're answer I think I read that too.
Sorry but I do not understand... shall I remove setting of `self._state` from the `send_key` method?
You already need to change the state in update, so it doesn't matter. let the code as it is.
Removed all settings of `self._state` from send_key method.
